client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: A nurse reviews safety practices for hazardous-drug preparation. Which statement about a properly ventilated safety cabinet is accurate?

options.A: It is an engineering control used during hazardous-drug preparation, and appropriate personal protective equipment is still required
options.B: It replaces the need for personal protective equipment during hazardous-drug preparation
options.C: Its primary purpose is to store medications after compounding is complete
options.D: It is used mainly to increase compounding speed rather than reduce exposure

rationale: NIOSH recommends properly ventilated safety cabinets for hazardous-drug preparation and separately directs that appropriate personal protective equipment be provided and used. Thus the cabinet functions as an engineering control but does not replace PPE. B incorrectly treats the cabinet as a substitute for PPE, while C and D misstate its safety purpose.
educational_objective: Recognize a properly ventilated safety cabinet as an engineering control for hazardous-drug preparation that supplements, rather than replaces, appropriate personal protective equipment.
source_organization: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Engineering Controls Database — Control of Exposure of Healthcare Workers to Hazardous Drugs
source_version_date: NIOSH page last reviewed November 16, 2018; current CDC/NIOSH page accessed 2026-08-17

source_claim_supported: Properly ventilated safety cabinets are engineering controls for hazardous-drug preparation, and appropriate PPE remains required rather than being replaced by the cabinet.

correction_summary: Removed the overbroad original claim that a biological safety cabinet universally protects both personnel and the preparation for all hazardous or sterile materials. Rebuilt the item around the directly supported NIOSH hazardous-drug safety principle that a properly ventilated safety cabinet is an engineering control and does not replace PPE. The NCSBN 2026 hazardous-materials blueprint was pinned exactly.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by NIOSH. B contradicts the separate PPE requirement; C confuses a safety control with storage; D misstates the purpose of the control. The corrected item avoids unsupported cabinet-class/product-protection generalizations. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
